newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan traders eye profits from insurance business.
newsitem.headline: Japan traders eye profits from insurance business.

text.p: Japanese trading firms said on Monday they expect to gain profits from the insurance brokerage business in Japan amid deregulation in the industry.

Itochu Corp, Sumitomo Corp Nissho Iwai Corp and Marubeni Corp said they have plans to start or expand their insurance-related businesses through possible tie-ups with U.S. and European insurance brokers.
Itochu said it started jointly operating a life insurance brokerage with a Japanese insurer in April. The firm added it planned to form a separate non-life insurance brokerage.

"Itochu has been active in the insurance brokerage business for more than 20 years overseas. Now we can engage in this business in Japan as deregulation is taking place," an Itochu spokesman said. The trading house plans to more than double its pre-tax profit in its insurance division in the year to March 31, 2001, to 2.5 billion yen, he added.
Sumitomo said it set up a brokerage to offer life and non-life insurance products last September.
"There could be a possible tie-up with foreign companies in the future because they have more experience," a Sumitomo spokesman said.
Nissho Iwai said it expected to begin non-life insurance broking operations by July 1998.
Marubeni also said it was aiming to start a non-life insurer brokerage business this year, adding there was a possibility it would link up with foreign brokerages.
Itochu, Sumitomo and Nissho Iwai already operate as insurance brokers overseas through their subsidiaries, they said.

In April 1996, brokers were permitted to act as intermediaries in the sale of insurance products of various insurers. Up until then, sales offices were only able to sell products of a particular insurer.
